name: Serbia
summary: Serbia is not in the EU, so EU citizens need a residence permit too. There is no investor visa and no dedicated digital nomad visa. Permits are issued on grounds such as employment, owning a company, owning residential property (no minimum value), study or family, as a single permit for up to 36 months. Permanent residence comes after 3 years and citizenship 3 years after that.
naturalisation: Three years of continuous permanent residence (itself after 3 years of temporary residence), plus release from the previous citizenship; Ministry of Interior has discretion.
dual_citizenship_note: General route requires release from the previous citizenship (or an undertaking to renounce); dual citizenship is possible by marriage to a Serbian citizen or for persons of Serbian descent.

routes.name: Single permit (residence and work) on employment
routes.summary: A single permit covers residence and work together for up to 36 months, renewable, on the basis of an employment contract.
routes.requirements: Employment contract and employer registration; residence and work combined in one permit up to 36 months (Law on Foreigners as amended July 2023, in force 1 February 2024, per law-firm sources). Applications are online.
routes.physical_presence: Residence in Serbia; absences up to 10 months in total or 6 at once are tolerated for continuity

sources.title: Law on Foreigners Serbia: Key Changes in 2026

routes.name: Residence as owner of a company or entrepreneur
routes.summary: Foreigners can found a company (d.o.o.) or register as an entrepreneur and receive a single permit on that basis; the business must show real activity.
routes.requirements: Registration with the Serbian Business Registers Agency (APR) with actual activity; permit up to 36 months. Capital and income thresholds not published in the sources used.

sources.title: Law on Foreigners Serbia: Key Changes in 2026

routes.tax_note: A permit does not decide tax residence; Serbia uses a 183-day and centre-of-interests test.
routes.name: Temporary residence on property ownership
routes.summary: Owning a residential building or flat in Serbia that the foreigner lives in is a recognised ground for a temporary residence permit. There is no minimum property value.
routes.requirements: Residential property in the applicant's name that the applicant lives in; 'no minimum property value applies' (private.law wiki). Official text not read. Income or means proof not sourced.
routes.physical_presence: Same continuity rules; visa-free days do not count

routes.name: Freelancer / remote worker (self-employment permit, no nomad visa)
routes.summary: Serbia has no dedicated digital nomad visa; remote workers register a sole proprietorship or company and apply for a single permit. Guides disagree on the income needed.
routes.requirements: Serbian preduzetnik or d.o.o. needed to work legally; Serbian bank account, health insurance; income figures in guides conflict (about EUR 3,500 a month in one, other figures elsewhere), so none is recorded.
